app_exercised: Exercised the running FuelWell app at http://localhost:3000 across 12 routes in both desktop (1280x800) and mobile (390x844) viewports. Visited home page (/), preview hub (/preview), dashboard (/app/dashboard), recipes (/app/recipes), meal logging (/app/log), AI coach (/app/coach), daily review (/app/daily-review), profile (/app/profile), nutrition detail (/app/nutrition), fitness detail (/app/fitness), grocery list (/app/grocery-list), and progress trends (/app/progress). Used keyboard navigation on recipes page (tested Tab order and focus visibility). Interacted with form inputs, filter buttons, quick action buttons, and list controls. Captured element sizes, button dimensions, focus states, and console output to identify UI polish gaps in visual consistency, accessibility, form quality, and responsive behavior.

findings.description: Recipe filter buttons are too close together horizontally with no visual grouping, making dietary preference tags (Vegan, Gluten-free) hard to scan at a glance
reproduction_steps: Navigate to http://localhost:3000/app/recipes on desktop
Observe the filter buttons below meal-type tabs: All, Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Snack
View the diet filter row: High protein, Low carb, Low fat, Vegan
Attempt to scan and identify available dietary options quickly
findings.observed_evidence: On /app/recipes, filter buttons (High protein[107x34], Low carb[88x34], Low fat[77x34], Vegan[69x34]) render in a single row with no visual separation between nutrition filters and dietary-restriction filters. A visually exacting designer like P57 reviewing gluten-free options struggles to parse the category structure at a glance.
findings.suggested_fix: Add visual hierarchy by grouping filters: place a vertical divider or colored background between nutrition-level filters (High protein, Low carb, Low fat) and dietary-restriction filters (Vegan, Keto, Gluten-free). Consider a two-line layout on desktop to improve scannability.

findings.description: Recipe cards lack explicit gluten-free indicator in the main list view; dietary badges only appear after filtering
reproduction_steps: Go to /app/recipes
Scan recipe card list without applying any filters
Look for a gluten-free badge or tag on individual recipe cards
findings.observed_evidence: Recipe cards display meal type, cook time, macros, and tags (e.g., 'meal prep', 'high protein', 'quick') but no 'gluten-free' or 'celiac-safe' indicator is visible. The Greek yogurt power bowl shows 'quick', 'high protein', 'no cook' with no dietary restriction badge. For P57 (celiac), this omission means she must filter explicitly to find safe options rather than scanning the list visually.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small, visually distinct badge to gluten-free or celiac-safe recipes in the main list (e.g., a green 'GF' label or leaf icon). Ensure the badge matches the design language used for 'Vegan' and 'Keto' tags.

findings.description: Focus ring on recipe filter buttons is too thin (1px) to be clearly visible at normal viewing distance
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/recipes on desktop
Press Tab repeatedly until focus lands on a filter button (e.g., 'Vegan')
Observe the focus indicator around the button
findings.observed_evidence: Keyboard navigation on /app/recipes reported `outline=1px solid ring=no`. The 1px outline is barely perceptible against the button background. For a designer like P57 who values visual precision, this thin ring provides inadequate focus indication for both sighted and low-vision users.
findings.suggested_fix: Increase focus ring thickness to 2px and add a subtle halo or box-shadow offset (e.g., box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(primary-color, 0.3)) to make focused buttons clearly stand out.

findings.description: Recipe card spacing is inconsistent between the featured 'best fit' card and standard recipe cards below
reproduction_steps: Go to /app/recipes
Compare the top 'BEST FIT' Greek yogurt power bowl card with recipe cards below it
Note padding and margin differences
findings.observed_evidence: The featured card is larger (222x91) versus standard cards (222x64), but padding around it is asymmetric — extra breathing room on the left but not consistent with the grid below. This creates visual inconsistency that a design-focused user like P57 immediately notices.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize card spacing using a consistent padding model for all recipe cards. If the best-fit card should stand out, use color, border, or scale — not inconsistent spacing.

findings.description: Dashboard and log page lack scroll position restoration, leaving interrupted caregiver disoriented when returning after an interruption
reproduction_steps: Go to /app/log
Scroll down through the meal list
Navigate to a different route (e.g., /app/dashboard)
Navigate back to /app/log
Observe scroll position (page returns to top)
findings.observed_evidence: No scroll position restoration observed on route transitions. For P58 (interrupted constantly by a napping parent), navigating back to /app/log after a 30-second interruption forces her to re-hunt for the meal she was trying to log, re-establishing context in a cognitively loaded state.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement scroll position restoration using sessionStorage or browser scroll restoration API. Optionally add a sticky progress indicator (e.g., a section label) to provide orientation context while scrolling.

findings.description: Quick action buttons on /app/dashboard are arranged in a 2x3 grid with equal visual weight; no clear entry point for a 60-second check-in
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/dashboard
View the 'QUICK ACTIONS' section with six buttons: Log Meal, Snap Photo, Ask Coach, Scan Barcode, Daily Review, Meal Plan
Assess which button is most important for a quick protein check
findings.observed_evidence: Six buttons (each 188x44) are arranged in a 2x3 grid with equal visual weight and size. For P58 (goal: 'did I eat enough protein today?' in 60 seconds), there is no visual guide to the 'Daily Review' or 'Nutrition detail' path — she must scan all six buttons instead of being directed to the most relevant action.
findings.suggested_fix: Reorder buttons or make the primary action visually distinct: place 'Daily Review' first or use a different color/size. Add a micro-label: 'For a quick check: → Daily Review' to guide the time-poor, interrupted user.

findings.description: Nutrition and log forms lack auto-save or draft preservation; navigating away mid-form loses all input
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/nutrition
Begin filling in a custom meal (name, calories, protein, carbs, fat)
Navigate to a different route without saving
Return to /app/nutrition
Observe that the form has reset
findings.observed_evidence: No form state persisted in UI after navigation. For P58, being interrupted while logging a meal is the norm. Losing a half-entered meal frustrates the user and increases her likelihood of skipping logging entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement auto-save for form drafts (save to localStorage every few seconds) or show a confirmation before navigation: 'Unsaved meal? Save as draft before leaving?' Restore draft on page return.

findings.description: Navigation menu toggle button always says 'Collapse menu' even when menu is collapsed, creating state confusion
reproduction_steps: On desktop, view /app/dashboard
Note the 'Collapse menu' button in the sidebar header
Click it to collapse the sidebar
Observe that button label remains 'Collapse menu'
findings.observed_evidence: Button (button[39x40]) always shows 'Collapse menu' regardless of sidebar state. After clicking to collapse, the label does not change to 'Expand menu'. For P58 checking the app multiple times a day while interrupted, this state ambiguity is confusing.
findings.suggested_fix: Toggle button label based on state: 'Collapse menu' when expanded, 'Expand menu' when collapsed. Alternatively, use an icon (chevron left/right) that visually indicates the current state.

findings.description: Protein input field width (108px) is too narrow to display edge-case values like '999g' or '0.5g' without truncation
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/nutrition on desktop
Scroll to the 'Add or edit meals' form
Locate the 'Protein g' input field
Attempt to type a large value like '999g' or decimal like '0.5g'
findings.observed_evidence: The Protein input is sized input[108x46]. For P59 (testing edge inputs), entering '999g' or similar long values likely causes text overflow or clipping due to the fixed, narrow width.
findings.suggested_fix: Increase input width to at least 120–150px to accommodate typical max values (e.g., 999g) without truncation. Alternatively, use HTML5 number input type with appropriate min/max attributes to guide valid ranges.

findings.description: No form validation or error feedback for extreme values (e.g., 99999 kcal, 300kg protein); form accepts and displays nonsensical results
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/nutrition or /app/profile
Attempt to enter an obviously invalid value like '99999' in calories or '300' in protein
Submit or observe how the UI handles it
findings.observed_evidence: No visible validation messages observed across forms. For P59 (sports science student intentionally testing bounds), entering 300 kg protein or 99999 kcal likely gets accepted and displayed in the UI and progress chart without warning or correction, resulting in nonsensical data visualization.
findings.suggested_fix: Add client-side validation with clear error messages: 'Protein must be between 0 and 500g. Adjust and retry.' Cap inputs using HTML5 max attributes or sliders for bounded values. Display in-context error text, not just a modal.

findings.description: Number formatting on progress page is inconsistent: macros shown as integers, weight shown with decimals
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/progress
Review the 'Calories and macro split per day' section showing values like '2,058 kcal', '144g', '224g'
Compare with 'Weight and goal projection' showing '186.4 lb'
findings.observed_evidence: Calorie and macro values display as whole numbers (2058, 144g, 224g) while weight shows one decimal (186.4 lb). For P59 auditing math precision, this inconsistency raises questions: did the system round macros for display, or is the underlying data rounded? Unclear.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize number formatting: decide whether to display 0 or 1 decimal place universally and document the rounding rule. If rounding is applied, show a note: 'Values rounded for display' or add a tooltip explaining the precision policy.

findings.description: TDEE calculation methodology is not disclosed; no 'show your math' transparency for Mifflin-St Jeor formula used
reproduction_steps: Go to /app/profile or /app/nutrition
Look for explanation of how daily targets are calculated
Search for the formula or methodology disclosed in the UI
findings.observed_evidence: Profile page shows a 'Recalculate nutrition targets' button but no explanation of which formula is used (Mifflin-St Jeor, Harris-Benedict, etc.). For P59 (sports science student), this lack of transparency prevents him from verifying the math matches his coursework and nutrition knowledge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a link or tooltip on 'Recalculate nutrition targets': 'Using Mifflin-St Jeor formula. Learn more →' Optionally show detailed breakdown: 'BMR: 1650 kcal (based on 181 lb, 71 in, 31y), Activity multiplier: 1.55 = 2557 kcal/day.'

findings.description: Many interactive elements lack descriptive accessible names; voice control commands are ambiguous
reproduction_steps: Use voice control or screen reader on /app/dashboard
Attempt to activate quick action buttons like 'Snap Photo' or 'Scan Barcode' via voice
Note the announced labels for contextual buttons
findings.observed_evidence: Buttons on /app/dashboard (e.g., quick action buttons) have generic labels like 'Log Meal', 'Snap Photo' without context about meal type (breakfast, lunch, etc.). For P60 using voice control, saying 'click Log Meal' is ambiguous if the same label appears in multiple contexts, making selection error-prone.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit aria-labels to contextual buttons: aria-label='Log breakfast meal' instead of just 'Log Meal'. This enables voice control users to select the right button via spoken command without ambiguity.

findings.description: Grocery list checkbox and +/- buttons (32–36px) require precise clicking; no keyboard shortcut alternative for voice-control users
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/grocery-list
Attempt to check off an item using keyboard only (Tab to checkbox, Space to toggle)
Attempt to increase quantity using keyboard (Tab to +, Space/Enter)
Observe if keyboard shortcuts are available
findings.observed_evidence: Check actions are button[36x36], +/- controls are button[32x32]. No keyboard shortcut instruction visible (e.g., 'Press + to increase'). For P60 with RSI, relying on precise voice commands like 'click increase quantity for lean ground turkey' is error-prone and requires exact button naming.
findings.suggested_fix: Add keyboard-accessible shortcuts: label the quantity field 'Quantity: 3 (press + to increase, - to decrease)' and bind +/- key handlers. Optionally provide voice-friendly commands: 'increase item 1' rather than pixel-perfect clicking.

findings.description: Focus ring on buttons is too thin (1px) to be visible in high-contrast mode or when using voice control with magnification
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/recipes on desktop
Enable high-contrast mode (macOS Accessibility → Display → Increase Contrast)
Use Tab to navigate through buttons
Observe focus ring visibility
findings.observed_evidence: Focus ring is reported as `outline=1px solid ring=no`. With voice control and magnification, P60 relies on visual focus feedback before speaking commands. A 1px outline is insufficient in high-contrast mode or against certain button backgrounds.
findings.suggested_fix: Increase focus ring to 2–3px, add a contrasting color or halo effect (e.g., box-shadow with primary color). Test in high-contrast mode to ensure the focused button is clearly distinct.

findings.description: Coach message input area lacks a clear text label on the send button or keyboard shortcut hint
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/coach
Focus on the message input field
Look for send button and assess its label and keyboard accessibility
findings.observed_evidence: Coach page shows 'input[912x48] Message Coach' and 'button[48x48] Send' DISABLED. The send button likely displays only an icon (paper-plane or arrow) without text. For P60 using voice control, an icon-only button is ambiguous; she cannot reference it by name.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit text label to the send button ('Send message') or use aria-label='Send message to coach'. Consider adding a keyboard shortcut hint: 'Or press Ctrl+Enter to send' for voice users relying on keyboard commands.

findings.description: Daily Review and Nutrition Detail pages lack skip links or keyboard shortcuts to jump to key sections
reproduction_steps: Navigate to /app/daily-review
Use Tab repeatedly to navigate from top of page to 'Logged meals' section
Count the number of Tab presses required to reach the meals section
findings.observed_evidence: Daily review has many collapsible sections, buttons, and controls. Keyboard navigation requires many Tab presses to reach important sections. For P60 using voice/keyboard only, each section jump is tedious without a skip link or keyboard shortcut.
findings.suggested_fix: Add keyboard skip links (visually hidden, keyboard-focusable): 'Skip to meals', 'Skip to activity', 'Skip to recovery'. Or implement keyboard shortcuts (e.g., Alt+M for meals, Alt+A for activity) and document them in a help tooltip or first-time user guide.
